feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: International news, global reporting and analysis from NPR. Plus dispatches from NPR’s State of the World podcast.

entry.title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
entry.summary: The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.

entry.title: As UN Secretary General's last day approaches, search for his replacement continues
entry.summary: The UN Secretary General's term ends this year, but the big powers at the UN have been unable to agree on a replacement. UN watchers worry that there will be little time to get up to speed.

entry.title: Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and deputy secretary of state, has died
entry.summary: Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday. He was 80.

entry.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
entry.summary: As the fast-moving outbreak continues to spread in eastern Congo, fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting efforts to contain the spread of the disease.

entry.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
entry.summary: Leader Kim Jong Un reportedly visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons to cope with threats from the U.S. and South Korea.

entry.title: Storms disrupt Thanksgiving travel. And, FCC violated ABC's free speech, judge says
entry.summary: The East Coast's weather is a major concern this holiday, as it could lead to coastal flooding. And, the judge says the FCC can't punish ABC for satire Trump doesn't like.

entry.title: How American Thanksgiving took root — and evolved — in Liberia
entry.summary: The first settlers of Liberia were African Americans who brought along the holiday of Thanksgiving — which has evolved to reflect the history and identity of this new nation.

entry.title: Army to detonate tons of lead azide after delays. And, Abrego Garcia leaves U.S.
entry.summary: Authorities have evacuated a 5-mile radius to prepare to dispose of thousands of pounds of lead azide. And, after a nearly two-year legal battle, Kilmar Abrego Garcia's has voluntarily left the U.S.

entry.title: Republican wants FBI and CIA answers before questioning Nvidia chief
entry.summary: "The public is rightly concerned," says the Republican lawmaker, who wants to know what the FBI and CIA knew about potential national security threats and whether Jensen Huang was warned.

entry.title: Greetings from Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest point in all its splendor
entry.summary: Climbing tall mountains like Kilimanjaro is a study in contrasts — from beating sun to freezing nights, fire and snow.
